A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same H2DiLR research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including the additional material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original four-participant sEEG tone-decoding experiments, representation analyses, ablations, and CHB-MIT seizure-prediction results in Appendix C.1.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds an anatomical contribution analysis with numerical saliency scores in Appendix D and Table A4.

M1.justification: The principal two-stage H2DiLR procedure is unchanged. New Appendix D introduces an analysis-only single-stage adaptation combining H2D and neural decoding, applying cross-entropy through a Transformer decoder and straight-through gradient estimation. This is a limited procedural addition.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four-participant Mandarin tone-decoding recordings and CHB-MIT seizure-prediction dataset. Tables A5-A8 document the existing 407 stimuli; they do not establish expanded coverage. The anatomical analysis examines the retained tone-decoding setting.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and A3 retain the same SPaRCNet, FFCL, ST-Transformer, TS-TCC, CoST, NeuroBERT, and BIOT comparators, together with the same H2DiLR variants. The newly cited VQDNA work is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds an attribution protocol using class activation maps, channel saliency normalized to 0-1, and aggregation across anatomical regions, including reference regions. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged. Newly specified filtering and normalization details do not establish that the retained experiments changed.

E4.justification: Appendix D newly investigates which cortical and subcortical regions contribute to tone decoding, reporting ten regional scores in Table A4. This supplements the retained code visualizations, reconstruction examples, and partition, codebook, network-size, and participant-count ablations.

E5.justification: The five-random-seed evaluations and mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. The new anatomical table provides point scores without introducing additional run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table A4 adds normalized contributions, including 0.97 for Precentral Gyrus, 0.94 for Postcentral Gyrus, and 0.92 for Thalamus. Existing numerical entries in Tables 1-5 and A3 are unchanged, including H2DiLR's 43.67% average tone-decoding accuracy and 93.97% seizure-prediction accuracy.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, quantization rules, codebook updates, and objectives in Equations (1)-(8) are unchanged. The added attribution procedure supplies no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified decoding, homogeneity-heterogeneity disentanglement, 407-syllable coverage, and improved decoding performance. The anatomical analysis does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets Precentral and Postcentral Gyrus as key cortical contributors and highlights the Thalamus. It also explains the difficulty of attributing the original two-stage model and warns that the analysis-only adaptation may introduce instability and slight performance degradation. Existing principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 describes the reading materials generally and gives one sentence example; v2 supplies the complete 407-item character/syllable inventory and explains syllable prompts for uncommon characters. It also specifies the 300-Hz low-pass and 50/100/150/200-Hz notch filters, clarifies channel-wise seizure-data normalization, and identifies the hospital and review board. The complete stimulus specification substantially expands reproducibility information without establishing changed acquisition.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2024), VQDNA, and refines the implementation discussion's citations for masked modeling and VQ tokenizers. LaBraM's anonymous citation is consolidated under Jiang et al.; this is the same work. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording corrections, updates the publication header and corresponding-author information, and inserts Anatomical Region Contribution as Appendix D, renumbering the retained Broader Impacts section to E. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the anatomical contribution table A4 and stimulus tables A5-A8. Existing figures and tables retain their designs and contents, apart from limited caption and spacing corrections and page reflow. There is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The complete stimulus inventory and precise preprocessing disclosures reduce replication ambiguity. The anatomical analysis adds useful context and explicitly states its caveats, but its modified, potentially unstable single-stage model limits what it establishes about the original procedure. Benchmark evidence and the principal generalization limitations remain unchanged, making the overall improvement limited.
